TrickWork takes on GlimStone 3.5.1: Settings gains an Info tab with the version, an update check, the manual and a bug report, the Look tab sets every choice in one row, and the whole interface follows GlimStone's sizes and colours.

## ✨ Added

- Settings has a fourth tab, Info, with a Version card, a Help card and the About card, in that order.
- The Version card lists TrickWork and GlimStone, and each number links to its release page. Release notes opens the notes of the running version in a window, with a link to the release page. Check for updates asks GitHub for the newest release and shows the answer on the button itself: green when TrickWork is current, orange when a newer version is out, red with a shake when GitHub cannot be reached.
- The Help card has a Manual button that opens the documentation, and a Bug report button that saves a file you can attach to an issue. The file holds the versions, the platform, the language and your settings, but no images and no file names.

## 🎨 Design

- The look follows GlimStone 3.5.1.
- The Look tab puts every choice in one row, with the name at the start and the control at the end. Shape, theme and animations show a symbol beside each option, and System has one too.
- In rainbow mode each selector gets one colour of its own instead of one per option, and text keeps the single accent colour.
- Text follows GlimStone's five sizes. Body text is 14px, down from 15px.
- Every size given in rem now counts the browser's 16px, as GlimStone measures them, so buttons, gaps and fields come out a little larger and the README buttons exactly 160px wide.
- Settings is wider: its column grows from 48rem to 64rem as far as the window leaves room beside the brand card and Back.
- Warnings are orange instead of yellow, so yellow only marks what you can press or have picked.
- Filled buttons hover by stepping their colour instead of turning see-through, and every button gives a little when pressed. The three give buttons and their windows stay as they were.
- The character set's preset list stands beside its name, like the font list.
- The settings tabs, Back, Settings, the card grip and the preset buttons use the symbols GlimStone shares across its apps.
- The About card keeps the sentence about the project and the three ways to give. The report buttons moved to the Help card, and the version line to the Version card.

## ⚡ Improved

- The desktop app runs on Wails v3.0.0-beta.28, and the build tools and libraries are up to date.
